@graph.articleBody: The safest way to choose an SEO company is to ignore the promise and inspect the proof: what exactly it will do, what it can honestly claim, how it reports, and who owns what when the work is done. Anyone who guarantees a ranking is telling you something Google itself says nobody can sell. One disclosure before we start: Etuos sells SEO, so we have an interest in this topic. itemListElement.name: How to Choose an SEO Company Without Getting Burned

mainEntity.name: How do I choose an SEO company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ignore the guarantee and check the proof. Ask what exactly the company will do, what it will not promise, what its report includes and who will own your accounts. Compare two or three providers on the same questions, in writing.

mainEntity.name: Can an SEO company guarantee a first-page ranking?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google says there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking on Google, and that it does not guarantee it will crawl, index or serve your page. Treat a guaranteed position as a red flag.

mainEntity.name: What should an SEO report include?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your business results first, such as calls and form submissions, then Search Console numbers with their definitions: clicks, impressions, click-through rate and average position. It should also list the work done and the work planned next.

mainEntity.name: What are red flags when hiring an SEO company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Guaranteed rankings, secret methods, no list of tasks, near-identical city pages, reports without calls or inquiries, and a provider that wants to own your accounts.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to own my Search Console and Business Profile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you should. Google says a verified owner has the highest degree of permissions in Search Console. Have the provider work inside accounts that are in your name.
